core_obligations: Define the topology (proof lines 609-620): for an algebraic space X fix a surjective etale morphism p from a scheme U and declare a subset of |X| open exactly when its preimage in |U| is open; this is the quotient topology for the map on points.

Independence of the presentation (proof lines 622-648): for another etale chart U' -> X form the fibre product U'' = U x_X U'; all the maps in the resulting commutative square of sets are etale on schemes, the lower horizontal arrow is surjective and continuous, and the other three are surjective, continuous and open, so formally the map |U'| -> |X| is continuous and open; this also proves property (3) and shows the topology does not depend on the chosen presentation.

Continuity of morphisms (proof lines 650-672): for a morphism a : X -> Y choose presentations and a compatible square of schemes; all arrows except the one induced by a are known to be continuous and the vertical ones are surjective and open, which formally implies the continuity of the map |X| -> |Y|, giving property (2) and completing the uniqueness statement.
proof_roadmap: Define the topology through a presentation as a quotient topology.
Show independence of the presentation by a fibre product square with openness and surjectivity bookkeeping.
Deduce continuity of morphisms from a compatible square of presentations.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that there is a unique topology on the sets of points of algebraic spaces over a base with the three stated properties: agreement with the usual topology on schemes, continuity of the maps induced by morphisms, and continuity and openness of the maps induced by etale charts (statement lines 595-607). The proof (proof lines 609-674) defines the topology through one presentation as a quotient topology, shows independence of the presentation by analysing a fibre product square, and deduces continuity for arbitrary morphisms from a compatible square of presentations. H3: an original construction with a presentation-independence argument, written out in full.
